At FNBO, our employees are the heart of our story—and we’re committed to their success! Please see below the details of this career opportunity and how it fits into our organization’s success.

Summary Of The Job

The Sr. Director, Advanced Data Scientist will provide senior strategic and technical leadership within the Partnership Division's data science and modeling function. This role is responsible for defining and executing multi-year modeling roadmap and overseeing the development and implementation of advanced machine learning models that support credit decisioning and portfolio management. The successful candidate will combine deep quantitative expertise with the organizational influence and executive presence required to shape strategy, drive cross-functional alignment, and deliver measurable business impact at scale.

About This Role

• Vision and Strategy
• Define and own the multi-year modeling roadmap for the development of several critical custom credit-risk acquisition and portfolio management models, establishing strategic priorities, sequencing, and investment rationale aligned with Partnership Division business objectives.
• Serve as a senior thought leader and decision-maker on modeling approaches, leading discussions with senior business, credit risk, first line of risk, compliance, and technology stakeholders to align methodology, priorities, and risk considerations.
• Identify and evaluate emerging modeling capabilities, analytical approaches, and implementation methods that can expand the division's competitive advantage in credit decisioning and customer risk management.
• Communicate modeling strategy, project status, and key results to senior leaders through clear, executive-ready reporting — translating complex quantitative findings into actionable business insights and ensuring leadership has the visibility needed to make informed decisions.
• Model Development
• Independently design and develop advanced ML models for credit card acquisition and underwriting and account management and customer risk.
• Apply advanced statistical and machine learning techniques to large-scale customer and credit datasets.
• Evaluate and implement algorithms including gradient boosting, random forests, neural networks, generalized additive models, ensemble methods, survival models, and other advanced ML approaches.
• Conduct fair lending analysis (e.g., least discriminatory analysis).
• Identify opportunities to improve model performance, stability, interpretability, and business value.
• End-to-End Model Ownership
• Independently lead model-development projects from problem definition through production implementation.
• Translate business objectives into well-defined modeling frameworks, target variables, populations, and performance criteria.
• Perform feature engineering, variable selection, model development, hyperparameter optimization, and performance evaluation.
• Establish appropriate training, validation, and out-of-time testing strategies.
• Document modeling methodology, assumptions, limitations, and results.
• Partner with model validation and model risk management teams to address challenges and incorporate feedback.
• Advanced Analytics and Research
• Conduct research on emerging ML techniques and assess their applicability to credit risk.
• Develop innovative approaches for extracting predictive signals from traditional and alternative data sources.
• Investigate nonlinear relationships, interactions, customer behavior patterns, and temporal dynamics that may not be captured by traditional credit-risk models.
• Develop interpretable ML approaches that balance predictive performance with regulatory and business requirements.
• Explore techniques such as explainable AI, causal modeling, ensemble learning, semi-supervised learning, and automated machine learning where appropriate.
• Model Performance and Monitoring
• Develop model performance and stability monitoring frameworks.
• Monitor predictive performance, population shifts, variable stability, and model degradation.
• Identify emerging risks and recommend model recalibration, redevelopment, or replacement when appropriate.
• Conduct ongoing research to improve model performance and robustness.
• Technical Leadership
• Serve as a subject-matter expert in advanced ML and credit-risk modeling.
• Establish best practices for ML model development, testing, documentation, and deployment.
• Stay current with advances in machine learning, credit-risk analytics, and regulatory expectations.

Required Qualifications

The Ideal Candidate for This Role:

• Master's degree or PhD in Statistics, Data Science, Computer Science, Mathematics, Operations Research, Econometrics, or a related quantitative field.
• PhD strongly preferred, particularly for candidates with strong research experience in machine learning, statistics, or quantitative finance.
• 7+ years of experience developing statistical or machine learning models, preferably in financial services or consumer credit with experience developing credit card acquisition and account-management models.
• Strong experience independently developing predictive models using large and complex datasets.
• Demonstrated expertise in Python and/or R; strong SQL skills.
• Experience with gradient boosting/XGBoost/LightGBM, ensemble methods, neural networks, and other advanced ML techniques.
• Experience with model explainability techniques such as SHAP and partial dependence.
• Experience with the full model-development lifecycle, including development, implementation, and monitoring.
• Strong understanding of credit-risk concepts and consumer lending.

Candidates must possess unrestricted work authorization and not require future sponsorship.

Knowesis, Inc. is seeking an experienced Graph Data Scientist to support the Pandemic Response Accountability Committee (PRAC) by developing and applying advanced graph-based analytic techniques to detect fraud, waste, abuse, and mismanagement across federal programs. The PRAC delivers data-driven oversight of pandemic relief and OBBBA Act funds and works closely with federal Offices of Inspectors General (OIGs) and federal law enforcement to ensure that covered funds are used appropriately and not subject to fraud or misuse.

The Graph Data Scientist will play a critical role within the PRAC Analytics Center, applying graph theory, network science, and machine learning to uncover hidden relationships, detect complex fraud schemes, and support investigative case development. This position will contribute to PRAC's advanced analytic support, investigative intelligence, and capability development efforts by building graph models, knowledge graphs, link analysis products, and graph-based fraud detection tools.

The PRAC analytic platform operates in a cloud-based environment using tools such as Azure Databricks, Microsoft SQL Server, Microsoft Power BI, and neo4j, along with other advanced technologies to analyze and visualize public, non-public, and commercially available data. The Graph Data Scientist will work within agile sprints and Integrated Project Teams (IPTs), collaborating with PRAC stakeholders, OIG partners, and law enforcement to deliver high-quality analytic outputs that support oversight, investigative support, and continuous capability enhancement. The role requires strong technical expertise, analytic rigor, and the ability to translate complex graph-based insights into clear, actionable intelligence for diverse stakeholders.

Trust employees are not part of the civil service, nor does trust fund employment lead to Federal status. OVERVIEW
This position is located in Washington, DC, within the Forest Global Earth Observatory (ForestGEO), Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute (STRI), under the Office of the Under Secretary for Science and Research at the Smithsonian Institution (SI).

STRI provides a global platform for research on tropical forests and marine ecosystems, biodiversity, and human well-being.

The ForestGEO program is a global network of scientists and forest research sites dedicated to advancing the long-term study of the world's forests.

The GEO-TREES initiative builds on this network to improve the accuracy and verification of global forest carbon estimates through collaboration among forest research sites worldwide. The Data Scientist supports the Forest Global Earth Observatory (ForestGEO) and GEO-TREES programs as a liaison between site-based data collection and the development of analytical data products.

Data Management, Scientific Analysis, and Software Programming (50%)

• Performs data-management, computational, and bioinformatics assignments supporting research in tropical biology, ecology, and forestry.

• Develops, implements, modifies, and maintains data-processing pipelines used to process plot-based tree inventory and related ecological data and to derive estimates such as forest woody biomass density.

• Evaluates the performance of existing data-processing pipelines and recommends modifications or improvements based on data characteristics, analytical requirements, user needs, and experience working with ForestGEO and GEO-TREES site teams.

• Develops and modifies computational procedures for analysis of ForestGEO and GEO-TREES scientific data using established data-science principles, methods, and practices.

• Supports the archiving and long-term management of scientific datasets to ensure appropriate organization, documentation, accessibility, and usability.

• Develops and maintains data-management solutions and informatics workflows for data acquisition, formatting, validation, processing, analysis, use, and storage.

• Implements established data standards and contributes to the development and modification of data structures and architectures appropriate to assigned projects.

• Writes, tests, documents, troubleshoots, and maintains computer code used in data-processing and analytical workflows.
